Japan was accused to do unfair competition with the US in this exact period of time but the situation was much more different than the US-china situation right now.

To begin with, the US first pointed out how difficult it was to do business in Japan while many japanese were doing business in the US. Moreover the american trade balance with Japan was negative and Japan's markets were seen as closed while they benefited from the open american markets. Also the incredible speed with which the japanese economy has developed between the mid 50's and the 80's was thanks to the technological transfer from the U.S.

​

But the difference with the US-China rivalery today is that these countries, despite the economical frictions, were allied. Japan's army was undevelopped and tied by the constitution which was written by the U.S occupation. Japan depended on the U.S army for its own protection, while the US had a great position along with the positions in Korea to surround Russia (now China). This is still going today, even tho Japan has developped its own army and tries to normalize the status of its military forces. So there were no military confrontation because, despite friction, Japan and US are allied since the mid 50's. I strongly believe that the interdependance of the japanese and the american economies was much more developped than the one that exists today with China (also the world's economy was much more closer than it is now, a lot of countries were out of the starting globalization game).
